body:
Try:
```gdscript
var e = InputEventKey.new()
e.keycode = which_key | KEY_MASK_ALT
e.alt_pressed = true
```

The shortcuts in the editor use this format

I tried:
```gdscript
func _enter_tree() -> void:
	_working_button = add_control_to_bottom_panel(_control1, 'works', _make_alt_shortcut(KEY_1))

	var e = InputEventKey.new()
	e.keycode = KEY_2 | KEY_MASK_ALT
	e.alt_pressed = true

	_broken_button = add_control_to_bottom_panel(_control2, 'nope')
	_broken_button.shortcut = e
```
but the shortcut (alt+2) still doesn't work.  I don't think the shortcut is invalid since the shortcut for `_working_button` does work and it's made the same way as the shortcut for `_broken_button` in the original code.

I probably didn't do exactly what you meant, so I tried this:
```gdscript
func _make_alt_shortcut_other_way(which_key):
	var e = InputEventKey.new()
	e.keycode = which_key | KEY_MASK_ALT
	e.alt_pressed = true

	var sc = Shortcut.new()
	sc.events = [e]
	return sc
```
and neither shortcut worked when I used this to create the shortcuts.

This is a documentation issue, as it is documented for `EditorDock` (the new method of creating docks, you are using a deprecated method) that shortcuts are only updated when the dock is added. If it breaks compatibility this is probably undesired

If you are looking to create a plugin I would recommend using `EditorDock` as it provides more customizability, including the ability to make your docks floating or move to the side panels built in. You should just need to add an `EditorDock` as the parent of your current node and call `EditorPlugin::add_dock()`

>  If it breaks compatibility this is probably undesired

This was found in an existing plugin (GUT).  I gave `EditorPlugin::add_dock()` a try using the MRP project and it isn't suitable yet for bottom docks.  There doesn't appear to be a way to put a dock back to the bottom after it has been moved to one of the side docks (when initially set to `dock.default_slot = EditorPlugin.DOCK_SLOT_BOTTOM`).  The bottom dock "button" is not enabled when right clicking the dock tab or using the three vertical dots button.  Godot remembers where the dock was last, so even closing the dock and relaunching Godot then using the shortcut key to show the dock puts the dock back on the side and not in the default location.

The GUT plugin doesn't have a layout that works well with side docks at this time.  I would like to be able to prevent it from being moved to a side dock.  It at least has to be able to be put back into the bottom dock after being moved.

I'm not sure how far along `add_dock` is.  I usually don't start testing new Godot versions until they hit Beta.  I can create issues for the new way of doing it if it's supposed to be feature complete.

I wasn't aware that `add_to_bottom_panel` was deprecated since 4.0 (at least the "Making plugins" page doesn't reference it).

I was able to get the panel to work as expected using the properties and flags of `EditorDock`.

I was also able to update the shortcut by freeing the existing dock and recreating it with the new shortcut.  It's a little clunky but it works.  

```gdscript
var my_dock_ctrl := ColorRect.new()
var my_dock

# called from wherever we need to change the shortcut.
func change_shortcut(new_shortcut : Shortcut):
	my_dock.remove_child(my_dock_ctrl)
	remove_dock(my_dock)
	my_dock.queue_free()
	_add_bottom_panel_dock_with_shortcut(new_shortcut)

func _add_bottom_panel_dock_with_shortcut(shortcut : Shortcut):
	my_dock = EditorDock.new()
	my_dock.title = "My Dock"
	my_dock.dock_shortcut = shortcut
	my_dock.default_slot = DOCK_SLOT_BOTTOM
	my_dock.set_global(false);
	my_dock.set_available_layouts(EditorDock.DOCK_LAYOUT_HORIZONTAL | EditorDock.DOCK_LAYOUT_FLOATING);

	my_dock.add_child(my_dock_ctrl)

	add_dock(my_dock)
```

If we're updating documentation then https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/plugins/editor/making_plugins.html should be updated to not reference `add_control_to_dock`

The function has been deprecated since 4.5 or 4.6 I believe, so it is a rather recent deprecation.

You shouldn't need that extra function as shortcuts for EditorDocks update instantly, rather you should be able to just set the shortcut property (unless that didn't work, in which case that is probably a bug)

```gdscript
# called from wherever we need to change the shortcut.
func change_shortcut(new_shortcut : Shortcut):
	my_dock.dock_shortcut = new_shortcut
```

I agree with not referencing add_control_to_dock.
